user.title: Alert Redux
user.description: Set up Alert Redux alerting. Global defaults can be changed afterwards in the integration's options.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Only a single configuration possible.

menu_options.manual: Manual: fired and dismissed by actions
menu_options.state: State: an entity is in a given state

manual.title: Add a manual alert
manual.description: A manual alert is fired and dismissed by the `alert_redux.fire` and `alert_redux.dismiss` actions.

data_description.name: Shown on the card and used as the notification title. The entity ID is derived from it when the alert is created.
data_description.priority: Sets the alert's colour and sort order.
data_description.icon: Leave empty to use the priority's default icon.
data_description.acknowledgeable: Turn off for alerts that must not be silenced.
data_description.user_dismissable: Show a dismiss button on the card. The dismiss action always works, whatever this is set to.
data_description.subject_entity: Optional. The entity the alert is about, for use in messages. Leave empty to use the watched entity, if there is one.

notifications.name: Notifications and messages
notifications.description: Who is notified, how often reminders are sent, and what the messages say.

data_description.use_default_groups: Send to the default notifier groups set in the integration's options. Turn off to choose this alert's own groups.
data_description.notifier_groups: Used when the default groups are turned off. Leave empty to notify nobody.
data_description.use_default_reminders: Use the default reminder schedule set in the integration's options. Turn off to set this alert's own.
data_description.reminder_schedule: Used when the default schedule is turned off. Minutes between reminders while the alert is firing and unacknowledged, e.g. `10, 20, 30, 60`: the last gap repeats. Leave empty for no reminders.
data_description.message: Optional. Sent when the alert starts firing, and shown on the card. A template: it can use `name`, `subject_entity_name`, `fire_count`, `fire_data`, `duration`, and entity states. Leave empty for the default: the alert's name, followed by "is firing."
data_description.display_message: Optional. A different message for the card, if the on message isn't what you want shown there. Also a template.
data_description.reminder_message: Optional. Sent as a reminder while the alert is still firing. A template, as for the on message; `duration` is how long it has been firing. Leave empty for the default, which gives the name and that duration.
data_description.done_message: Optional. Sent when the alert stops firing. A template, as for the on message; `duration` is how long it fired, and `end_reason` is `resolved`, `dismissed`, or `no_data`. Leave empty for the default.

state.title: Add a state alert
state.description: A state alert fires while an entity is in a given state, e.g. a door sensor is `on`.

data_description.name: Shown on the card and used as the notification title. The entity ID is derived from it when the alert is created.
data_description.priority: Sets the alert's colour and sort order.
data_description.icon: Leave empty to use the priority's default icon.
data_description.target_state: The alert fires while the entity is in this state, e.g. `on` or `open`. Targeting `unavailable` or `unknown` alerts on that state; otherwise those states mean the alert has no data.
data_description.condition: Optional. A template that must also render true for the alert to fire; when it stops being true, the alert ends.
data_description.delay_on: Optional. How long the condition must hold before the alert fires.
data_description.delay_off: Optional. How long the condition must stay false before the alert stops firing. Absorbs brief flickers.
data_description.acknowledgeable: Turn off for alerts that must not be silenced.
data_description.subject_entity: Optional. The entity the alert is about, for use in messages. Leave empty to use the watched entity, if there is one.
data_description.no_data_grace: Optional. How long a firing alert keeps firing while its inputs have no data. Leave empty to use the global default.

user.title: Add a notifier group
user.description: A notifier group is a set of notifiers that alerts send to. Add at least one member.

data_description.name: How alerts and the options refer to this group.
data_description.loud: Turn on for notifiers that make a noise, such as speaker announcements. Quiet hours (a later release) will apply to loud groups only.
data_description.entities: `notify` entities. They receive the message, and the title if they can show one.
data_description.actions: Legacy `notify.*` actions, such as `notify.mobile_app_phone`. These can take extra `data` (e.g. a mobile notification channel; its values can be templates using the message variables) and a `target`. You can enter an action that isn't loaded yet.
data_description.persistent: Also create a Home Assistant persistent notification.

error.name_exists: A notifier group with this name already exists.
error.no_members: Add at least one member: a notify entity, a legacy action, or the persistent notification.
error.action_missing: Each legacy notify action needs its action set.
error.invalid_data: A legacy action's data must be a mapping of keys to values.

fire.name: Fire
fire.description: Fires a manual alert. Firing an alert that is already firing adds to its fire count and keeps its acknowledgement.

data.name: Data
data.description: Variables made available to the alert's message templates as `fire_data`.

ack.name: Acknowledge
ack.description: Acknowledges a firing alert, stopping its reminders until it stops firing.

unack.name: Remove acknowledgement
unack.description: Removes an alert's acknowledgement, so that it is active again.

not_manual.message: {entity_id} isn't a manual alert, so it can't be fired or dismissed by action.

data_description.no_data_grace: How long a firing alert keeps firing while its inputs have no data, unless the alert sets its own.
data_description.startup_delay: When Home Assistant starts, wait this long before evaluating condition alerts. Zero to evaluate straight away.
data_description.default_groups: The groups alerts send to unless they choose their own. With none set, those alerts send to a persistent notification instead.
data_description.default_reminder_schedule: Minutes between reminders while an alert is firing and unacknowledged, unless it sets its own, e.g. `10, 20, 30, 60`: the last gap repeats. Leave empty for no reminders.

error.invalid_schedule: A reminder schedule must be a list of positive numbers of minutes, e.g. `10, 20, 30, 60`.

default_groups_unset.title: No default notifier groups are set
default_groups_unset.description:
{count} alerts use the default notifier groups, but none are set, so their notifications go to a persistent notification instead: {alerts}.

To fix this, add a notifier group, then choose it as a default in the Alert Redux integration's options (Settings > Devices & services > Alert Redux > Configure). Alternatively, give each alert its own notifier groups.
